rationale: DERIV_EXPORTS_KOT4. Kotlin has NO `export` keyword — measured, not asserted: script/m14/kotlin-exports-probe.ts enumerated 260 distinct node types over 782 code-bearing corpus files and not one expresses an export declaration. What the language DOES have is a visibility surface (1,173 visibility_modifier nodes in the same 782 files; private 721, public 279, internal 134, protected 39) plus a public-by-default rule. So the export surface is a derivable fact about the file, and the analyzer already computed it into the `exports[]` channel — which NO consumer reads (parallel-indexer only knows `relType === "exports"` on a relationship row). This fixture pins the edges on the channel the store reads, and pins the exclusions: `internal` is module-visible rather than consumer-visible, a member is reachable through its owner rather than exported as a name of its own, and `via` distinguishes a written `public` from the implicit default so a consumer can tell which fact decided it. The source is `(file)` with metadata.fileLevel (the M60/#910 contract); a package name was rejected because the store's own defensive export filter drops a lowercase dotted source, so every such edge would be deleted at insert time.
